headline: High: Kestra can overwrite shared files and exfiltrate workflow data; the prompt-engineering repo adds no isolation or verification layer.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing repo with no runnable I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. B can read/write files and emit stdout, but there is no documented shared channel or parser bridge between them. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste or an external orchestrator, which is unusual and low blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B’s output into A as prompt text, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between A and B, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Do not paste B output into A without sanitizing it.
Disable any shared clipboard or message bus between the two.
Add a provenance tag to any text passed from B to A.
requires-engineering: add an orchestrator filter that strips instructions from B output.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B has broad filesystem and network egress, so if it receives sensitive workflow data it can transmit it outward. A is a docs-only content repo with no data classes touched, so it is not itself a leak source, but it also provides no containment or redaction. The pair therefore creates a default leakage path through B when shared inputs are present.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in B's workspace, B can read and transmit them.
IF A is used to generate prompts containing secrets and those prompts are fed to B, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of B's workspace.
Mount only the minimum files B needs.
Turn off outbound network access for B when handling sensitive data.
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for A.
requires-engineering: add content redaction before B egresses data.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has unrestricted filesystem write plus subprocess and shell execution, and its docs show multiple instances are supported. A has no runtime capabilities, so it does not mitigate contention. If both are pointed at the same directory or mutable artifacts, B can overwrite or race on shared state, creating destructive conflicts by default once co-located.
conditions: IF A and B share any writable directory, B can overwrite A's files.
IF multiple B instances target the same path, race conditions can corrupt artifacts.
mitigations: Give B a private writable directory.
Make A read-only.
Avoid running multiple B instances against the same path.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add per-task workspace isolation.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a prompt-engineering content source, so its outputs may be treated as guidance by B if an operator wires them together. B can then act on those inputs by writing files, sending notifications, or triggering cloud/SSH tasks. A provides no verification mechanism, and B’s orchestration surface makes downstream mistakes plausible in default automation setups.
conditions: IF A's text is used as workflow instructions for B, B may execute incorrect actions.
IF B is configured to send email, Slack, or cloud actions from A-derived inputs, errors cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before B executes A-derived instructions.
Separate A-generated guidance from B-executable workflow files.
Add validation checks on B inputs.
Log and diff A-to-B handoffs.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for all A-produced artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for A, while B exposes logs, artifacts, and notifications across many external services. Because A is docs-only and not a data processor, the compliance risk is mainly that B’s broad integrations could carry regulated data if the operator routes it there. The other agent is not cited for a direct compliance violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through B's external integrations, compliance obligations apply.
IF retention or residency requirements are imposed on B's logs or artifacts, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through B integrations.
Review B retention settings before use.
Restrict B to non-regulated workflows.
Document data flows for logs and artifacts.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
